newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Call sellers in ADT.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Call sellers in ADT.

text.p: Investors were selling calls in ADT Ltd, particularly the April 25 calls, after it said it agreed to be bought by Tyco International Ltd in a stock deal valued at $5.6 billion.
The deal values ADT at $29 per share, which compares with Western Resources Inc's hostile bid of $22.50 a share.
ADT shares were up 3-5/8 at 25-3/8 in late U.S. trading. Tyco fell 2-1/2 to 57-3/4 and Western Resources was ahead 5/8 at 30-3/4.
The ADT April 25 call was the most active ADT option, with about 3,475 contracts changing hands.
The ADT April 25 call had open interest of just 180 contracts through last Friday, so nearly all the volume Monday was position openings.
"We're thinking they already own the stock," William Johnson, a market maker at the CBOE, said of the April 25 call sellers.
"So they're making money on the move today and they they're just going to sell some premium against it," he said.
He added that the only other action of note was in the March 22-1/2 calls, which traded 940 contracts. He said investors were selling those out, taking profits.
Johnson said volatility in the ADT options had been climbing recently as speculation grew that either Western Resources would raise its bid or another company would come in with a competing offer.
"We felt they were either going to raise it or someone was going to come in like this," he said. "We were waiting for something to happen."
Western Resources, ADT's largest shareholder with a 27 percent stake in the electronic security and vehicle auction company, launched its hostile takeover attempt three months ago.
ADT had rejected the offer as inadequate.
Western Resources said Monday it was studying Tyco's bid.
Tyco chairman L. Dennis Kozlowski said he expected the merger with ADT to boost Tyco's fiscal 1998 earnings by $0.20 a share, or $50 to $52 million, above Wall Street estimates.
He said he expected the deal to be finalized by June 30.
Tyco options were moderately active, with most activity on the call side. The Tyco April 55 call was most active, with volume of nearly 600 contracts.
Options on shares of Western Resources were not busy. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
